Reference Text: A study finds that “gatekeeper” mutations make enzymes called kinases more active by destabilizing them in their inactive form, which may explain more aggressive cancer recurrence

Structure of the FGFR kinase showing the locations of the gatekeeper residue in the blue, hydrophobic spine in yellow, and ATP in cyan. Most drugs bind to the kinase in the same pocket as ATP. 
Structure of the FGFR kinase showing the locations of the gatekeeper residue in the blue, hydrophobic spine in yellow, and ATP in cyan. Most drugs bind to the kinase in the same pocket as ATP. Credit: Traaseth Lab/NYU
More than 70 FDA-approved cancer drugs are kinase inhibitors, which work by blocking kinases—enzymes that add phosphate groups to molecules in the cell—and preventing the chemical activity necessary for signaling and growth in cancer cells. Kinase inhibitors can be very effective, but long-term, some patients experience aggressive recurrences that are more difficult to treat and resistant to the original drug. 

A new study by New York University researchers, published this week in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, explains why cancers not only stop responding to kinase inhibitors but come back stronger, a finding that could inform which drugs oncologists use as a first-line treatment. 

A leading cause of drug resistance—when cancer no longer responds to a kinase inhibitor— is the emergence of genetic mutations, particularly those in a region in the kinase called the “gatekeeper” residue. The gatekeeper is deeply embedded in the kinase and allows or prevents access to an even-deeper hydrophobic (or water-repelling) pocket.

Reference Text: When we think of steel, we often imagine tall skyscrapers and large-scale constructions – heavy industry. But in the realm of music, steel can play a more delicate role.

In comes the triangle. Remember the triangle? You may have first encountered the simple instrument in grade school, as a tinkering tool to play with for band practice. It is often disregarded as a legitimate instrument and forgotten about, but the percussive idiophone should not be taken for granted.

Unassuming in composition (it is literally an outline of a triangle), it is one of the only percussion instruments that is made entirely out of metal. It is usually shaped from a steel bar into an equilateral or isosceles triangle, with an opening at one of its corners.

Historically, the triangle was created from both solid iron and steel rod, but is now primarily made from steel. It comes with a playing apparatus, usually a steel beater, and hangs suspended from a fishing line. The thin suspension line lets the instrument vibrate freely and create its signature noise.

The simple triangle’s sound is affected by the sizes and materials it comes in; the preferred orchestra size is between six to nine inches in diameter and played with a steel or wooden beater, which dictate a distinct note. The instrument’s tones range diversely from a shimmering trill to a more substantial, all-encompassing ring, all depending on what the conductor wants.

The triangle was first introduced into the world in the 16th century, but it is actually a descendent of the ancient Egyptian percussion instrument called the sistrum, which was used for worship and other religious purposes. Percussion instruments were originally meant for three main purposes: religious ceremonies, military signals, and dance.

Now, the triangle is a permanent member of the modern orchestra, originally used as a way for composers to add a bit of a sparkle to their music. Out of all the musicians, the triangle player has the most unnerving role within a composition. They cannot risk trial entry during a performance since the tone can linger, so they must be very careful to make sure they play the right note at exactly the right time.

Domestic abuse can take on many forms including physical, sexual, or emotional abuse and can occur when a person intentionally causes physical or emotional harm to a family member or cohabitant. Emotional, or verbal abuse, can include:

Repeated threats
Attempts to embarrass
Belittlement
Coercion
Attempts to restrict action

What Differentiates Abuse From an Argument?

There are numerous factors which can separate an argument or disagreement from abuse. While couples may disagree over the best way to solve a problem, in cases of abuse, one partner will engage in actions that seek to establish control over their partner.

For example, if a couple is engaged in an argument, physical abuse can occur when one person strikes or hits their partner to ensure that they get their way. An example of emotional abuse is when a person attempts to block their partner from participating in a decision through belittlement or by insulting their intelligence.  Another indication of abuse is the existence of a pattern of behavior. As emotional abuse is psychological in nature, patterns of conduct play a large role in determining abuse. Arguments can often bring feelings of anger and frustration to the surface and couples may resort to insults or may act uncharacteristically.

This type of behavior may become abuse when it is a constant factor in disputes. For example, if one spouse repeatedly tells their partner that their opinions are dumb or invalid, these actions may constitute verbal abuse. Reference Text:  Is a domain of materials science and engineering that studies the physical and chemical behavior of metallic elements, their inter-metallic compounds, and their mixtures, which are known as alloys. Metallurgy encompasses both the science and the technology of metals; that is, the way in which science is applied to the production of metals, and the engineering of metal components used in products for both consumers and manufacturers. Metallurgy is distinct from the craft of metalworking. Metalworking relies on metallurgy in a similar manner to how medicine relies on medical science for technical advancement. A specialist practitioner of metallurgy is known as a metallurgist.
The science of metallurgy is further subdivided into two broad categories: chemical and physical metallurgy. Chemical metallurgy is chiefly concerned with the reduction and oxidation of metals, and the chemical performance of metals. Subjects of study in chemical metallurgy include mineral processing, the extraction of metals, thermodynamics, electrochemistry, and chemical degradation (corrosion).[1] In contrast, physical metallurgy focuses on the mechanical properties of metals, the physical properties of metals, and the physical performance of metals. Topics studied in physical metallurgy include crystallography, material characterization, mechanical metallurgy, phase transformations, and failure mechanisms.
Historically, metallurgy has predominately focused on the production of metals. Metal production begins with the processing of ores to extract the metal, and includes the mixture of metals to make alloys. Metal alloys are often a blend of at least two different metallic elements. However, non-metallic elements are often added to alloys in order to achieve properties suitable for an application. The study of metal production is subdivided into ferrous metallurgy (also known as black metallurgy) and non-ferrous metallurgy (also known as colored metallurgy). Ferrous metallurgy involves processes and alloys based on iron, while non-ferrous metallurgy involves processes and alloys based on other metals. The production of ferrous metals accounts for 95% of world metal production.
Modern metallurgists work in emerging and traditional areas as part of an interdisciplinary team alongside material scientists and other engineers. Some traditional areas include mineral processing, metal production, heat treatment, failure analysis, and the joining of metals (including welding, brazing, and soldering). Emerging areas for metallurgists include nanotechnology, superconductors, composites, biomedical materials, electronic materials (semiconductors), and surface engineering.  Reference Text: A few decades ago, the idea that there could ever be too much choice was, for some, a controversial claim. It ran against cultural narratives especially in the United States and classic economic theory that assumed having more options was always better than having fewer. A larger assortment of alternatives, so conventional wisdom went, gave each of us a better shot at finding something that better satisfied our preferences. And, if any of the additional options didn’t appeal to us, we were free to ignore them.

Yesterday’s conventional wisdom no longer seems so conventional today. Over the past few decades, a large body of research has repeatedly shown that when people experience choice overload when they face more options than they desire they can experience a wide range of negative outcomes, from frustration and confusion to regret, dissatisfaction, and even choice paralysis.

Yet the story of how the number of choices we have affects our decision-making is about to take another turn. In a recent study with over 7,000 participants from six countries, we found that choice deprivation a feeling of not having enough to choose from not choice overload is the most common consumer experience in both trivial and highly consequential domains. And choice deprivation isn’t just more common it’s also more harmful to choice satisfaction than overload.
    
For many of us, the phenomenon of choice overload resonates with our everyday experiences of decision-making. How often, for instance, does a seemingly simple trip to the grocery store become overwhelming when we face aisle after aisle of options? And that’s not to mention the impossible burden of sorting through limitless products when shopping online or choosing a home to buy that meets all our criteria. Choice overload has even achieved a cultural influence that is rare for scientific ideas, earning mention in sources as varied as long-running TV drama Grey’s Anatomy and Torrey Peters' bestselling novel De-transition, Baby.

Reference Text: Rules of origin determine where goods originate, i.e., not where they have been shipped from, but where they have been produced or manufactured. As such, the 'origin' is the 'economic nationality' of goods traded in commerce. The tariff classification, value, and origin of goods are determining factors based on which the customs tariff treatment is applied. For customs matters, there is a distinction between two types of origins, notably non-preferential origin, and preferential origin.

Non-preferential rules of origin are used to determine the country of origin of goods for applying the most-favored-nation treatment and for implementing several commercial policy measures such as anti-dumping and countervailing duties, trade embargoes, safeguard measures, and quantitative restrictions or tariff quotas. They are also used for trade statistics, public tenders, and origin marking. The EU applies its own set of non-preferential rules of origin provisions, which may differ from any other third country.

Preferential rules of origin determine whether goods qualify as originating from certain countries for which special arrangements and agreements apply. Where all the requirements are met, goods with preferential origin can be imported with lower duty rates or at zero rates, depending on the preferential tariff treatment provided.

BOIs are decisions by the competent authorities, which are binding on the holder and the customs authorities in all Member States in respect of goods imported or exported after their issue, provided the goods and the circumstances determining the acquisition of origin are identical in every respect to what is described in the BOI. The BOI decisions are usually valid for three years from the issue date. It is to be noted that the holder of a BOI is not exempted from presenting the necessary proof of origin to be granted a preferential duty rate. In the international context, BOI decisions are called advance rulings on origin.

But the question can still be raised even on the abundant conception as the question whether existence is a property of individuals involved in our talk of what exists and what does not, which is then a question about the logical form of the sentences used in our existential discourse. 

We can trace the issue of whether existence is property to a disagreement between the ancient Greek philosopher Aristotle and some of his medieval followers over the relationship between an individual’s essence and its existence. Some of a thing’s properties are contingent in that it might not have had them. I am writing right now, but I might have been out for a run instead. But first, a local news station wanted to do a story about Ghost's life in the wild and his rescue. The news soon made headlines across the nation, and that's when things got complicated.
A Las Vegas family who says Ghost is theirs, and that his name is really Hades, came forward to claim him. The women who trapped Ghost didn't believe the family, leaving the two sides in a bitter feud that culminated this past weekend with a confrontation involving police.

Living in the wild
Ghost was first spotted in July by Henderson residents who saw him running with a pack of three coyotes. Residents would post videos and photos of him from time to time on a neighborhood Facebook group, tracking his movements with keen interest. 

Then last month a resident named Judy Hendrickson saw that Ghost was limping heavily and shot a video of him. 

That's when a two-woman crew calling themselves the Southern Nevada Trapping Team say they knew they had to intervene and capture Ghost for fear the pack would turn on him. 

In all, Ghost lived among the coyotes for at least six months and it showed. He's got bite scars all over his face and body, he had a broken toe (which was causing the limp and needs amputated), and his scrotum was so badly infected, a veterinarian said it would have to be removed altogether, said Carole Sandy, a board member with Amor Paludo Animal Rescue, which had taken charge of Ghost's care and potential adoption.

The surgeries would cost thousands, and a GoFundMe page raised more than $14,000 to pay for it.

Modern laboratory mice, as we know them today, were born from over a century of careful breeding and selection for desirable traits in research. The ancestor of the modern mouse arose in the 1900s, on a farm in Illinois, where a woman named Abbie Lathrop imported mice from the Far East to Europe and North America and bred them. She was the first person to create an inbred mouse strain, quite different from its wild cousins.

Inbred strains of mice have been particularly useful to research. Produced through inbreeding and mating of brother/sister pairs over at least 20 generations, inbred mice are very similar. They have nearly identical DNA, with very little variation. This blank, stable, reliable canvas, is perfect for scientific experiments.

The differences observed between inbred mice is more likely to be a product of their environment than differences in individual mice. The fact that all mice within an inbred strain are genetically similar reduces experimental variability and increases study reproducibility, whilst also enabling transplants between mice without risk of rejection.

Over the years, researchers created thousands of different inbred but also outbred mouse strains, which have defined genetic backgrounds and unique characteristics such as coat color, behavior, metabolism, fertility, immune function, and other physiological traits. Natural mutations from inbred strains that are prone to obesity, cancer, or defects in their immune system soon began to emerge, fuelling a deeper understanding of disease and biology.

Reference Text: 3 Reasons Why Smart Technology Is Making Us Less Productive. 

I love technology that makes work, and life, a little easier. I love that my Apple Watch will remind me when it's time to take out the trash or pick up my daughter from soccer practice. Here's the thing though, I probably shouldn't have to depend on a $400 piece of smart technology to remind me to, you know, show up.

The downside is that I've noticed that as our dependence on technology increases, our actual productivity decreases. I think technology is good at making it easier to stay busy, but being busy isn't the same thing as being productive. Here's why:

1. Notifications are technology's drugs. 

Every app on my phone wants to send me notifications. It's great because they all have so much important information they need to share with me to help me be more productive. Except, all I do all day is tap icons with red dots like a digital version of whack-a-mole, trying to get rid of all the notifications. Research shows that this constant stimulation of our devices raises dopamine in our brains, which means they are like drugs.

2. It's making us dumber.

It's true, technology has allowed us to do some pretty incredible things. I can't argue with the fact that it has allowed us to solve previously insurmountable problems, but at a very basic level, all of this smart technology has made us dumb. I think it's because of how much we now depend on it for even the most basic things. 

Here's the thing. If you don't use a muscle, after a while you'll lose it.  Sure, it's not technically a muscle, but if you stop using your brain because your watch tells you when it's time to go to a meeting, stand up, or use the bathroom-- you're not getting any smarter, right? 

3. We connect with technology, not people.

Have you ever sat in a restaurant and looked around? Of course not, the last time you were in a restaurant you were busy looking at your phone. But if you had, you would have seen a bunch of other people who were doing the same thing. A room full of people, all sitting at tables with presumably other people they know and have some level of affection for, staring at an illuminated screen.

Reference Text: A chamber of commerce is an association or network of businesspeople designed to promote and protect the interests of its members. A chamber of commerce is often made up of a group of business owners that share a locale or interests but can also be international in scope. They will choose leadership, name representatives, and debate which policies to espouse and promote. Chambers of commerce exist all over the world. They do not have a direct role in creating laws or regulations, though they may effectively influence regulators and legislators with their organized lobbying efforts.

The first chamber of commerce was founded in France in 1599. The first one in the United States started in New York in 1768. The United States Chamber of Commerce was founded in 1912 and promotes pro-business issues via lobbying efforts at the national level. At the state, city, regional, and local levels, chambers focus on issues and advocacy relevant to their membership. Such chambers may or may not be affiliated with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce through a Federation Partnership Program. The national chamber tends to support conservative politicians. The largest lobbying group in the U.S. Chambers of Commerce differs from trade groups or associations promoting a specific industry. Among the benefits chamber members receive are deals and discounts from other chamber members, listing in a member directory, and various other programs and services designed to promote business activity in a region.

Chambers of commerce also play an important role in promoting business activity and representing chamber members in local municipalities. At least at the local level, chamber of commerce members often meets to discuss and attempt to shape policy related to the business and overall economic environment. Members also receive the distinction of being a preferred local vendor and listing on various municipal websites and literature.

Many chambers of commerce rely on membership dues as their primary source of revenue. Most chapters offer various membership levels at different prices with different benefits for their members. Every member is required to pay dues, which help cover the organization's overall operating costs. Chambers may also hold fundraising events to raise additional funds or require the special purchase of tickets to attend their events.

Reference Text: There are plenty of studies arguing that handwriting is better for notetaking than typing. There are plenty more studieshowever, suggesting that handwriting does not have that many advantages over typing. Many professors ignore the issues of accessibility. What is strain rate sensitivity?

Strain rate sensitivity is a measure of how quickly a material responds to a change in stress. The higher the strain rate sensitivity, the faster the material will change under load. Low strain rate sensitivity means the material is less likely to fail catastrophically, while high strain rate sensitivity can lead to sudden failure.
Provide a scale of low to high strain rate sensitivities using different orders of magnitude.
Low strain rate sensitivity can be in the range of 0.01 to 0.1. Mid-range strain rate sensitivity is 0.1 to 0.3. High strain rate sensitivity is above 0.3.
What are some methods for measuring low strain rate sensitivities?

The traditional test method for strain rate sensitivity is called “creep” testing. During creep testing, a sample of the material is subjected to a constant stress for a set period of time, and the resulting change in shape or size is measured. The faster the material deforms, the higher the strain rate sensitivity. Other methods for measuring strain rate sensitivity include dynamic mechanical analysis and nanoindentation.
Using nanoindentation, what are different methods for measuring both low and high strain rate sensitivites?

There are two basic methods for measuring strain rate sensitivity using nanoindentation: load-controlled and displacement-controlled. In the load-controlled method, the sample is tested at a fixed strain rate, and the resulting load vs. indentation depth curve is used to calculate strain rate sensitivity. In the displacement-controlled method, the sample is tested at a fixed displacement rate, and the resulting stress vs. indentation depth curve is used to calculate strain rate sensitivity. Both methods can be used to measure both high and low strain rate sensitivities.

The VAE architecture consists of an encoder neural network that maps input data to a latent representation, and a decoder neural network that maps the latent representation back to the input space. The VAE is trained using variational inference, which seeks to minimize the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the approximate posterior distribution over latent variables and the true posterior distribution. The KL divergence used to train variational autoencoders (VAEs) is an information-theoretic loss term that measures the difference between the approximate posterior distribution over latent variables and the true posterior distribution. During optimization, the KL divergence term acts as a regularizer that encourages the approximate posterior to approximate the true posterior as closely as possible. This helps to ensure that the encoded latent representation is rich and informative, while also avoiding overfitting. The KL divergence can also lead to a so-called "information bottleneck", in which the encoded representation is very simple and highly compressed. This is often desirable in applications where only a low-dimensional summary of the input data is needed.

Sharding is a technique used in blockchain to increase the processing power and transaction speed of a network by dividing the network into smaller, parallel sub-networks, or “shards”. Sharding allows the network to handle more transactions simultaneously, which improves performance and scalability. Each shard is managed by a set of shard validators, who verify transactions and produce new blocks.
what are shard validators

Shard validators are nodes in a sharded blockchain network who are responsible for verifying transactions and producing new blocks. They are selected based on a specific algorithm, and are responsible for maintaining the integrity of the network by ensuring that transactions are valid and that new blocks are produced correctly. Shard validators also participate in consensus algorithms to determine the order in which transactions are processed, and to decide which transactions are included in a new block.

Cross-shard communication in blockchain refers to the ability of different shards in a sharded network to communicate with each other. This is necessary in order for the network to function properly, as each shard needs to be able to verify transactions and produce new blocks, and also for the shards to reach consensus on which transactions to include in a new block. There are a variety of protocols and algorithms used for cross-shard communication, which vary depending on the specific blockchain implementation.
Consistency in sharding

Consistency in sharding refers to the fact that each shard in a sharded blockchain network must consistently produce valid blocks that are in agreement with the other shards. This is necessary in order for the network to function properly, as each shard must be able to verify transactions and produce new blocks, and also for the shards to reach consensus on which transactions to include in a new block. cap theorem

What are the distortions used in thought restructuring exercises in CBT?

Cognitive distortions are basically patterns of flawed thinking. There are many types, and a wide variety of them are used in thought restructuring exercises in CBT. Some common ones are:
 

 -  All-or-nothing thinking
 -  Mental filter
 -  Over-generalization
 -  Disqualifying the positive
 -  Jumping to conclusions
 -  Magnification
 -  Emotional reasoning
 -  Self-fulfilling prophecy
Can you identify possible CBT cognitive distortions in a statement?

Sure, here’s an example statement: “I’ll never find a job because I’m not smart enough.” Here are some possible cognitive distortions in that statement:
 

 -  Over-generalization - The speaker is making a sweeping statement about their ability to find a job, when in reality it is very possible that they would find a job if they tried.
 -  Mental filter - The speaker is only focusing on the negative, while ignoring the positive (that they are smart enough).
 -  Absolute thinking - The speaker is making an absolute statement about their ability, when in reality there are many factors that could lead to their finding a job.

 -  Mental filter - The speaker is only focusing on the negative, while ignoring the positive (that they are not a terrible person).
 -  Magnification - The speaker is greatly exaggerating the negative effects of being a terrible person.
 -  Emotional reasoning - The speaker is using their emotions to make a judgment about their future, when in reality there are many factors that could lead to their being loved again.

What Is a Business Cycle?

A business cycle is a period of repeated fluctuations in economic activity, including increases in production and employment followed by decreases and periods of recession. These cycles typically last from 18 to 24 months, although they can also last much longer. They are caused by a variety of factors, including productivity and market trends, as well as the availability of credit and changes in consumer confidence.
What Are the Stages of the Business Cycle?

The business cycle follows four main phases, which are interrelated:
 

 • Expansion: When economic growth is strong, businesses are profitable, employment and income are increasing, and there is high consumer confidence.
 

 • Peak: When the economy reaches its peak, business activity begins to slow, and profits fall. Employment and incomes also fall, and there is a drop in consumer confidence.
 

 • Contraction: When business activity falls and unemployment rises, the economy is in contraction. During this phase, there is a fall in production, investment, and consumption, and there is a drop in consumer confidence.
 

 • Recovery: When the economy begins to pick up again, the contraction phase ends and the recovery phase begins. Consumer confidence begins to rise, and employment and incomes begin to increase.
How Long Does the Business Cycle Last?

The business cycle typically lasts from 18 to 24 months, although it can last longer or shorter than that. During the contraction phase, the economy may be in recession for some time before the recovery begins. Similarly, the expansion phase may continue for some time after the peak.
What Was the Longest Economic Expansion?

The longest economic expansion occurred in the U.S. between 1991 and 2001, lasting for 10 years. During that period, there was very strong economic growth and a very low unemployment rate. Similarly, the longest recession on record was between December 2007 and June 2009, lasting for 18 months.

What does this error mean? Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'https://s.edkay.com/api/sync/1/?json=%7B%22token%22%3A%225c0c64023fb8062832eea2c3a91242d7%22%7D' from origin 'https://www.counselingdegreesonline.org' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.

This is a browser security feature called "CORS" (Cross Origin Resource Sharing), which prevents scripts running on one website from making unauthorized requests to other websites. In this case, the web page at "https://www.counselingdegreesonline.org" attempted to load a script from "https://s.edkay.com/api/sync/1/?json=...", but the requested script did not include the necessary "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header, so the request was blocked. Note that the script requested from "https://s.edkay.com" would have been permitted to run if it was located on the same origin (i.e. same domain and port) as the web page, since the same origin policy only applies to cross-origin requests.
When did the CORS security feature start?

The specific feature of the browser security model known as "CORS" was introduced in 2006 by the W3C, as part of the XMLHttpRequest Level 2 (XHR2) specification. However, the core principle of restricting cross-origin resource sharing to only permitted requests was originally introduced by Netscape as a way of allowing cross-origin framing without allowing arbitrary script access to the target origin. Note that despite the name, the same origin policy is not really a "policy" in the sense of an explicit rule, but rather a fundamental security assumption built into the browser security model. So if a script attempts to make a cross-origin request that does not include the "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" header, the request will be blocked.

define Flooding in terms of Computer Networks

In computer networking, flooding is a protocol for delivering data from a source to a destination, via intermediate nodes. It works by having each node that receives the data forward it to all of its neighboring nodes. This continues until the data reaches the destination. Flooding is a simple and reliable method for data delivery, but is not very efficient, as it requires each node to transmit the data multiple times.
define Tunneling in terms of Computer Networks

In computer networking, tunneling is a technique for enabling communication between two network nodes that are not directly connected. It works by encapsulating the data from one node in a packet, and then sending it through intermediate nodes to the destination node. When the packet arrives at the destination node, it is unpacked and the original data is extracted. Tunneling is a very efficient method for communication between unconnected nodes, as it requires only a single data transfer from each intermediate node.

parallel computing, why parallel computing, goals of parallel computing, applications, advantages and limitatons of parallel computing

The idea behind parallel computing is that many problems can be solved much more quickly by having multiple computing tasks run simultaneously, rather than having them run one after the other in sequence. The main goals of parallel computing are to reduce the amount of time it takes to run a computation, and to enable computations that would be impossible with conventional sequential computing. Parallel computing is useful for a wide range of applications, including scientific simulations, database querying, and web searching. Parallel computing has both advantages and disadvantages. On the plus side, it can significantly speed up computation; on the downside, it can be more difficult to program for, and requires special hardware and software.
types of parallelism: data, bit, instruction, task

Parallel computing can be categorized according to the types of parallelism it uses. The most common types of parallelism are: data parallelism, bit parallelism, instruction parallelism, and task parallelism.
 

 

 Data parallelism: In data parallelism, multiple copies of a program are run simultaneously, with each copy operating on a different set of data. This type of parallelism is useful for problems that can be split into many independent subproblems.
 

 Bit parallelism: In bit parallelism, multiple computations are performed simultaneously on different bits of the same data. This type of parallelism is useful for problems that can be split into many independent subproblems, where each subproblem operates on a different bit of the data.
 

 Instruction parallelism: In instruction parallelism, multiple instructions are executed simultaneously. This type of parallelism is useful for problems that can be split into many independent subproblems, where each subproblem is a relatively simple computation that can be performed in parallel.
 

 Task parallelism: In task parallelism, multiple independent computations are performed simultaneously. This type of parallelism is useful for problems that are composed of many small, independent computations.
speedup of parallelism, amdahls law and its formula

The speedup of parallelism is the ratio of the amount of time it takes to run a computation serially, versus the amount of time it takes to run the same computation in parallel. The speedup of parallelism is typically between 1 and 2, since parallelism is only partially effective at speeding up computation. The speedup of parallelism is governed by Amdahl’s law, which states that the speedup of parallelism is limited by the amount of work that cannot be parallelized. The speedup of parallelism is equal to 1/((1-p)+p/n), where p is the fraction of the work that can be parallelized, and n is the number of processors.

Describe the action taken by the kernel to context switch between processes with suitable diagrams

The kernel stores information about each process in a separate process control block (PCB), which includes information about the process’s state, registers, and memory usage. When a process needs to be switched out, the kernel saves its PCB in a process queue, and then chooses another process to run, pulling its PCB from the head of the queue.  First, we notice that the equation can be factored as:
 

 x^3 + ax^2 - x - a = 0
 

 = (x^3 + a x - a) - a
 

 = (x - a/2)^3 - a
 

 = (x - a/2)^2 * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2)^2 * (x - a/2) - a
 

 Second, if we plug in for the first factor, we get:
 

 (x - a/2)^2 * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 Third, if we factor the second factor, we get:
 

 (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 Finally, if we expand out the final factor, we get:
 

 (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2)^2 * (x - a/2) - a
 

 Now we can plug in for the first factor:
 

 (x - a/2)^2 * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 Finally, if we factor the last factor, we get:
 

 (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 So now we have:
 

 (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2)^2 * (x - a/2) - a
 

 = (x - a/2)^3 - a
 

 = x^3 + a x - a
 

 = x^3 + ax^2 - x - a
 

 = x^3 + ax^2 - x - a = 0(where a is a constant)

Software versioning is the practice of attaching version numbers to software releases. Software version numbers typically include a major, minor, and patch version, where the major version number is incremented for incompatible changes, the minor version number is incremented for backward-compatible changes, and the patch version number is incremented for minor bug fixes. In general, a major version number change should be made for significant changes that might break backward compatibility, a minor version number change should be made for backward-compatible changes, and a patch version number change should be made for minor bug fixes. Other changes, such as changes to the user interface, documentation, or license, do not typically require a version number change.

what does it mean to attack a straw man

Attacking a “straw man” is a fallacy of logic in which an argument is constructed that is easy to defeat, and then defeated, rather than the most powerful form of the opponent’s argument. Typically, this fallacy consists of misrepresenting the opponent’s position, and then attacking that misrepresented position. A common example of this fallacy is arguing against a “straw man” version of the opponent’s position, instead of the real position. Another example would be to prove that the opponent’s position leads to an absurdity, but this absurdity is not a part of the opponent’s position. In the latter case, this is sometimes called a “question-begging fallacy”, because the opponent’s position is assumed in order to prove that it is false, thus begging the question.
Assuming what needs to be proved is question begging fallacy. What's an example of that?

Here are some examples of argument by question-begging fallacy:
 

 1. If you don’t believe in God, then who created the universe? This argument assumes that God is the creator of the universe.
 

 2. It is impossible for God to exist, because if God existed, then God would be responsible for all evil in the world. This argument assumes that God is responsible for all evil in the world.
 

 3. I know that a developing fetus is alive and has done nothing morally wrong, because it is innocent. This argument assumes that a developing fetus is innocent.

The second example is very poor. It is biologically and self-evidently true that a developing fetus is both alive and has done nothing morally wrong. The burden of proof is on those who would deny that a living organism is in fact alive, and that is not innocent when it has had no opportunity (or capability) to engage in any wrongdoing.

what is virtual memory, Address space, memory space

The virtual memory of a computer system refers to a method of organizing and addressing the physical memory of a computer in an abstract way, so that the virtual memory can be referenced in a simpler, more intuitive way. The virtual memory is essentially a kind of “mapping” of the physical memory of the computer into a “logical” memory space that can be referenced in a simpler, more intuitive way. Address space refers to the space of addresses used to reference the memory of a computer. Memory space refers to the space of memory addresses used to reference the memory of a computer.
Address Mapping Using Pages: pages & blocks, page frame

The physical memory of a computer is broken down into pages and blocks, so that each page of memory is associated with a specific address within the address space. The physical memory pages are then grouped into larger units called page frames, which are managed by the operating system. The pages within a page frame are referred to as “virtual pages”, and can be referenced in the virtual memory space using simple, intuitive addresses.
Assocative memory page table

The address space is stored in a table called the “page table”, which is an associative array that maps virtual page addresses to physical page addresses. The page table is used by the processor to translate virtual memory addresses into physical memory addresses, and thus allow access to the physical memory of the computer. The page table is stored in the computer’s memory, and is updated by the operating system in response to various events, such as process creation, memory allocation, and page faults.
page replacement, page fault

When a process needs to access a page of memory that isn’t currently in the computer’s physical memory, a “page fault” occurs, and the operating system must replace a different page of memory in order to make room for the requested page. The operating system uses a “page replacement algorithm” to determine which page to replace, and then updates the page table to reflect the new mapping of virtual to physical pages.
explain page replacement algorithm: LRU, FIFO, OPA

The most common page replacement algorithms are:
 

 - LRU (Least Recently Used): replaces the page that has been least recently accessed.
 - FIFO (First In, First Out): replaces the oldest page in the computer’s physical memory.
 - OPA (Optimal Page Algorithms): uses a more sophisticated algorithm to determine which page to replace, based on a variety of factors.

What were Pestalozzi's views on education?

Pestalozzi believed that all children have the ability to learn, and that education should be designed to bring out each child's innate potential. He thought that children should be encouraged to develop their own interests and abilities, and that education should help them to become self-reliant, responsible, and productive members of society. He also believed that education should be individualized, and that it should meet the unique needs and interests of each child.
How did he arrive at these views?

Pestalozzi was influenced by the philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau, who believed that children are born with certain innate qualities that need to be developed in order for them to become healthy, happy, and productive adults. Pestalozzi also believed that children need to be actively involved in their own education, and that teachers need to be sensitive to each child's individual needs and interests. He believed that teachers should provide guidance and support, but should avoid being authoritarian or controlling. He believed that education should be child-centered, and that it should help children develop their own unique talents and interests.
Were his ideas accepted at the time?

Pestalozzi's ideas were somewhat controversial at the time, because they went against the prevailing view of education, which was much more authoritarian and focused on rote learning. However, his methods were gradually adopted by many schools, and today his view of education as child-centered and individualized is widely accepted.

 =ISERROR(VLOOKUP(A2, “your data range”, 1, 0))

Types of Databases

The different types of databases are relational, hierarchical, and network. A relational database is a set of facts (like a table) that can be related to one another, and is typically stored in a file. A hierarchical database is a tree structure that has a root node and a set of child nodes, and is typically stored in a file. A network database is a set of “nodes” connected by “edges” (like a graph), and is typically stored in a file.
Physical vs Logical Independence

Physical independence means that the physical storage of data is independent of the logical structure of data. Logical independence means that the logical structure of data is independent of the physical storage of data. There are several steps involved in normalization, which generally involve breaking down data into smaller “facts” and then combining these facts into larger tables. The main steps of normalization are as follows:
 

 -  1st normal form (1NF) - ensures that each record contains only one value for each field
 -  2nd normal form (2NF) - ensures that each field depends only on the primary key, and not on any other fields
 -  3rd normal form (3NF) - ensures that each field depends only on the primary key and not on any other fields, plus each non-key field depends only on the primary key
 -  BCNF - ensures that every field depends directly on the primary key
 -  relational normal form - various levels of normal form

In this example, several transcription errors could occur, including:
 

 1) Phonetic errors - This type of error results from the transcription program not being able to correctly recognize the speech patterns in the sentence. For example, if the speaker pronounced the word "doing" with a long "o" sound, the transcribed text might read "doin'."
 

 2) Omissions - This type of error occurs when the speech-to-text program fails to transcribe an entire word or phrase. For example, if the speaker paused briefly before saying "today," the transcribed text might read "how are you doing today."
 

 3) Insertions - This type of error occurs when the speech-to-text program transcribes an extra word or phrase that was not actually spoken. For example, if the speaker pronounced the word "doing" with a short "o" sound, the transcribed text might read "Hi, how are you doing today?"
 

 4) Word-level errors - This type of error occurs when the speech-to-text program transcribes a word incorrectly. For example, if the speaker pronounced the word "doing" with a long "o" sound, the transcribed text might read "Hi, how are you doing today?"

Explain the different space allocation methods for storing files on disks and the type of
 file access they support.

There are two main space allocation methods for storing files on disks: “contiguous allocation” and “extent-based allocation”. Contiguous allocation stores file data in contiguous blocks on the disk, while extent-based allocation stores file data in extents, which are segments of contiguous blocks. Contiguous allocation supports more efficient random file access, while extent-based allocation supports more efficient sequential file access.

What is a bad block? Describe the techniques to manage disk bad blocks. Or Describe
 the methods to handle bad block?

Bad blocks are disk blocks that have become unreadable or unwriteable due to physical damage to the disk surface. There are several techniques for managing bad blocks on a disk, such as: 1) disk remapping, which moves bad blocks to spare blocks on the disk; 2) “DMA” (direct memory access), which reads data from bad blocks directly into memory without writing to the disk; and 3) file-level bad block management, which marks bad blocks as unreadable or unwriteable and avoids using them when possible.
explain about the following: i. DMA ii. File control Block

i. DMA (direct memory access) is a technique for reading data from or writing data to a disk without using the CPU. DMA transfers data directly from the disk controller to memory or vice versa, so that the CPU is not involved in the data transfer. This can greatly increase the speed of disk I/O.  
 

 ii. File control blocks (FCBs) are structures used by an operating system to keep track of files on the disk. Each FCB contains information about the file’s name, size, and location on the disk. FCBs are used by the OS to locate and access files.

 steps involved in transforming an I/O request to hardware operations.

1. The I/O request is read from a program or from a higher-level operating system component.
 2. The I/O request is sent to the disk controller, which formats the request into a command.
 3. The command is sent to the disk drive, which performs the requested operation.
 4. The result of the operation is returned to the disk controller, which formats the result into a reply.
 5. The reply is sent to the higher-level operating system component or program that sent the I/O request.

What is PCA?

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a type of dimensionality reduction that is commonly used in data analysis. It allows you to take a set of high-dimensional data and to reduce it down to a lower-dimensional representation that still preserves the important information in the data.
How does the reduction really happens in PCA?

PCA works by performing an eigen-value decomposition on the covariances or correlation matrix of your data. This allows you to express your data in terms of a set of “eigen-values” and “eigen-vectors”, which are the principal components. The dimensionality of your data is then reduced by keeping only the leading (most significant) eigen-vectors, which capture the majority of the variation in the data.
What is mean by eigen value decomposition and covarince matrix?

Eigenvalue decomposition is a mathematical procedure for finding a set of “eigenvalues” and “eigenvectors” for a given matrix. The eigenvalues are the “principal components” that are associated with the matrix, and the eigenvectors are the corresponding “principal directions” in the data space. Thecovariance matrix is simply a matrix that contains the covariances of the variables in your data set. PCA performs an eigen-value decomposition on this covarianc matrix in order to find the principal components.

A database lock in Drupal refers to a situation in which one or more Drupal database tables are locked for exclusive access by one or more other processes or threads. This can occur if you have multiple users simultaneously editing the same content, or if you have multiple Drupal sites running on the same database instance. If you encounter a database lock, you can try to resolve it by freeing up the locked tables, either by forcing other processes to release the locks, or by freeing up the tables manually. Yes, Floyd-Warshall algorithm works on undirected graphs. It finds shortest paths between all pairs of nodes in the graph, by repeatedly updating shortest path distances using the shortest paths found so far. It does this using a “three-pass” algorithm, where it performs three iterations of updating shortest paths.

Which of these are you interested in?
Design smells

Design smells are defined as “a pattern that looks dubious”. So you might think of a design smell as a potential problem, or as an indicator that something could be improved. Some design smells are particularly common, and are a good indication that a design is probably not as good as it could be. Common design smells include:
 

 -  A large number of classes that all do similar things
 -  A lack of cohesion between classes
 -  Classes with many responsibilities
 -  A large number of arguments to a method
 -  Methods with many statements
Other common examples of design smells

In addition to the design smells I just mentioned, there are several other common examples. Some of these are specific to a certain programming language, while others are more general. For example, in Java, common design smells include:
 

 -  Having a class that’s too big
 -  Using interfaces that are too large
 -  Having many classes that all implement the same interface
 -  Using inheritance too much
Other common examples of design smells

Other common examples of design smells include:
 

 -  Large switch statements
 -  Looping over collections
 -  Long method names
 -  Unused parameters
Other common examples of anti pattern

Anti-patterns are defined as “a recognized pattern that is considered harmful”. So you might think of an anti-pattern as a pattern that you shouldn’t use. Common anti-patterns include:
 

 -  The singleton pattern
 -  The template method pattern
 -  The “god class” pattern
 -  The “god object” pattern
Other common examples of code smells

Code smells are defined as “an indication that code might be harder to understand or harder to maintain than it should be”. So you might think of a code smell as a potential problem with the code. Common code smells include:
 

 -  Having a method that’s too large
 -  Having a method that’s too complex
 -  Having many local variables
 -  Using inheritance too much
 -  Having a class with many responsibilities

What is market research?

Market research is the process of collecting information about target customers, their needs, preferences, and buying habits, and using this information to better understand the market for a product or service. This helps companies to make more informed decisions about product development, pricing, and advertising, and to better understand their customers and competitors. Market research is important for all businesses, but is particularly crucial for startups and small businesses with limited resources.
What is it called when someone does research on how organizations use certain technologies, processes, or methodologies?

This is called organizational research or organizational analysis. Organizational researchers study how organizations use technologies, processes, or methodologies, and how these choices impact the organization. This information can help organizations make better decisions about technology adoption, process improvements, and so on. Organizational research is important for all businesses, but is particularly crucial for organizations in rapidly-evolving industries, such as technology.
What kinds of job titles engage in organizational research or organizational analysis?

Organizational research and analysis is usually performed by market researchers, business analysts, and consultants. Market researchers typically conduct primary research using surveys, focus groups, and other methods to collect data on customer needs and preferences, competitors, and market trends. Business analysts use data collected by market researchers to identify patterns and trends in the market, and to develop recommendations for product development, pricing, and marketing strategies. Organizational analysts work with managers to identify problems within the organization and recommend solutions. These job titles may also be used interchangeably, depending on the organization.
So market researchers perform organizational analysis? How do they do this?

They also provide insights into potential future trends and market changes that the organization may want to take into account.
Is artificial intelligence ever used in market research?

Artificial intelligence is being used more and more in market research, especially in the areas of predictive analytics and natural language processing. Predictive analytics uses machine learning algorithms to analyze large amounts of data and predict future customer behavior. Natural language processing enables computers to understand human language, which can be used to analyze customer comments and feedback. Artificial intelligence is also being used in market research to automate surveys and focus groups, and to analyze large amounts of survey data more efficiently.

Overwhelm is an emotion which is experienced when a person feels overcome by circumstances or events, and is unable to cope or respond effectively. Overwhelm is typically associated with a range of negative feelings and experiences, including helplessness, anxiety, fear, and stress. The feeling of overwhelm can be very intense and disruptive, and may significantly interfere with one’s ability to function normally. Overwhelm can be caused by a variety of factors, including traumatic or stressful events, lack of sleep or rest, overwork or excessive responsibilities, and certain psychological disorders. use of larmor frequency in mri?

The Larmor frequency gives the basic precession frequency of protons in a magnetic field, and is used in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to obtain high resolution images of internal organs. In MRI, a strong magnetic field is applied parallel to the axis of the patient, and protons are excited at the Larmor frequency using radio frequency pulses. By measuring changes in the Larmor frequency due to proton interactions with surrounding tissue, high resolution images of tissue internal structure are obtained. The Larmor frequency is also used in nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) to measure nuclear magnetic resonance parameters.

what is Database Transaction ?

A database transaction is a group of statements that the database performs as a unit. For example, a transaction could consist of a number of inserts, updates, or deletions. These are commonly referred to as "SQL statements", because SQL is the most common language used for interacting with databases. A transaction has a "transaction state", which is either "active", "committed", or "rolled back". In order for a transaction to be committed, all of the statements in the transaction must be successfully completed, and the transaction must not have been rolled back. When a transaction is committed, all of the changes it made are made permanent.
what is Transaction states ?

A transaction can be in one of three states: "active", "committed", or "rolled back". An active transaction is one that has not yet been committed or rolled back. A committed transaction has been successfully completed and its changes have been made permanent. A rolled back transaction has been cancelled and its changes have been undone.
what is ACID properties ?

ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability. These are properties that a database must have in order to be considered "reliable". Atomicity means that all of the statements in a transaction are completed as a unit; either all of them are completed, or none of them are. Consistency means that the data in the database is always consistent; it never gets corrupted. Isolation means that transactions are isolated from each other, so that one transaction can't affect another transaction. Durability means that once a transaction has been committed, it's permanently stored in the database.
explain Concept of Schedule

A schedule is a list of the transactions that will be performed on a database. The schedule is used to determine the order in which transactions are performed, and to ensure that transactions are performed in a way that maintains the ACID properties of the database. There are a number of different schedules that can be used, including serial, parallel, and hybrid schedules.
